## Summary

I implemented support for custom block-level `<signature>` and `<stamp>` tags in the markdown conversion pipeline. All changes are in the source file `docling/backend/md_backend.py` (no test files touched).

### How it works

marko parses `<signature>TEXT</signature>` not as an HTML block but as a `Paragraph` containing `InlineHTML` open/close tags wrapping the inner text. So the existing HTML-block delegation path doesn't apply; I intercept these paragraphs directly.

### Changes made

1. **Imports** — added `PictureMeta`, `PictureClassificationMetaField`, and `PictureClassificationPrediction` from `docling_core.types.doc.document`.

2. **Recognition constants** — `_CUSTOM_TAG_CLASSES = ("signature", "stamp")` and a compiled regex to match the opening tags.

3. **Helper methods**:
   - `_collect_raw_text` — recursively gathers the text inside the tag (handles formatted content).
   - `_extract_custom_tag_block` — detects a paragraph wrapped by a matching `<signature>`/`<stamp>` open/close pair and returns `(class_name, inner_text)`, else `None`.
   - `_create_custom_tag_picture` — creates a picture element, sets `meta.classification.predictions[0].class_name` to the tag name, and attaches the inner text as a child `TextItem` with both `text` and `orig` set.

4. **Dispatch branch** — added at the top of `_iterate_elements` so a recognized custom tag closes any pending table, creates the classified picture, and returns early (skipping normal text/inline-group processing that would otherwise emit the tag as plain text).

### Verified behavior

- Document ordering preserved (text and picture elements interleaved as in the input).
- `<signature>TEXT</signature>` → picture with `class_name="signature"`, exports as `Signature\n\n<!-- image -->`.
- `<stamp>TEXT</stamp>` → picture with `class_name="stamp"`, exports as `Stamp\n\n<!-- image -->`.
- Inner text stored as a text child of the picture in both `text` and `orig` fields.
- Existing markdown backend tests still pass.

The `Signature`/`Stamp` labels and `<!-- image -->` placeholder in the export are produced automatically by `docling_core`'s markdown serializer from the `meta.classification` field — no serializer changes were needed.
